The Past Prospect Playbook

A step-by-step guide to finding the meetings that already exist in your CRM. One 7-business-day sequence you can run yourself, without buying a single new lead.

  1. Who goes on the list, who stays off it, and how many names to start with.

  2. What goes out each day, and why the timing works.

  3. Six emails, the short notes that go with them, and call and voicemail scripts.

  4. A reply for every answer you will get, including “later” and “stop”.

  5. How to confirm the meeting, remind them, and run it.

  6. A tracker for the window, plus a checklist and a note to send your compliance team.

How to get it: finish the 60-second fit check and we’ll email it to you, whether we’re a fit or not.

Why the calendar isn’t full yet

  1. 1

    Referrals are passive.

    They are your best source of clients, and you can’t schedule them. You wait.

  2. 2

    The CRM is full of people nobody works.

    Past prospects went quiet and nobody went back to them.

  3. 3

    The usual options are built around something else.

    Many agencies report on campaigns and impressions. Bought leads often go to several advisors at once. Software still needs someone on your team to run it. A vendor paid per meeting earns more by booking more.

What you need is simpler: a qualified person in front of your advisor on a set day.

Inside the PlaybookPreview

The 7-day schedule

  1. Day 1A short heads-up that a note is coming
  2. Day 2Email 1, the reconnect, and a call that afternoon
  3. Day 3Email 2, the recap
  4. Day 4A short reminder that asks for a reply
  5. Day 5Email 3, the update, and a second call
  6. Day 6Email 4, one more reason to meet
  7. Day 7Email 5, the final notice, and a third call. Email 6 closes the loop.

Our 90-day commitment

At least 15 attended, qualified meetings in your first 90 days from launch.

In your first 90 days from launch, we commit to at least 15 attended, qualified meetings that match your written criteria. If we’re short, we keep working at our cost (no operating fee) until you’ve taken 15 such meetings.

Written into your services agreement

The commitment depends on three things from you

  • Agree on your ideal client and the messages at kickoff
  • One advisor or owner on the weekly call
  • Follow the process we set for booked meetings

A qualified meeting is with a prospect who fits your written asset minimum, niche and geography, is a decision maker or co-decision maker, and attends live. You set the criteria in advance. The 90 days start at launch, so compliance review time does not count against them.

Founding rate

No setup fee. No per-meeting fees.

  • Initial term: 3 billing cycles, about 90 days. Then it renews every 4 weeks.

The math

Three cycles at $5,000 is $15,000. Set against the 15 meetings we commit to, that is $1,000 per attended, qualified meeting. If we’re short 90 days after launch, we keep working at our cost (no operating fee) until you’ve taken 15.

Whether that works for your firm depends on your own numbers. We run them with you on the call.

Questions

Do you sell leads?

No. We book attended first meetings for your firm only. Nothing is shared with another advisor.

We’ve tried agencies before. Why is this different?

Many agencies sell a campaign and report on activity: sends, clicks and views. We are judged on one thing: attended, qualified meetings. You see one number every week, so if it isn’t working you know early, not six months in.

How does compliance work?

Your compliance team approves every outreach message before it is sent. Outreach is by email and LinkedIn only, from domains and inboxes in your firm’s name that your firm owns. The compliance decision stays with your firm.

Per-meeting vendors booked us junk. What stops that here?

Two things. The fee is flat, so we are not paid more for booking more. And you set the criteria in writing before we start. Only attended meetings that match them count toward the 15.

What counts as a qualified meeting?

A prospect who fits your written asset minimum, niche and geography, is a decision maker or co-decision maker, and attends live.

What does it cost?

The founding rate is $5,000 every 4 weeks. No setup fee and no per-meeting fees. The initial term is 3 billing cycles, about 90 days.

Is $5,000 every 4 weeks worth it for a firm our size?

We work it out on the call with your numbers: your close rate on first meetings and your average new client size. If the math doesn’t work for your firm, we’ll say so.

What do you need from us?

A kickoff call, access to your CRM, sign-off on your ideal client and the messages, and one advisor or owner on a short weekly call. Your advisors need room for the meetings.

What happens after the fit check?

You pick a time for a 20-minute call on Google Meet. It ends with a yes or a no. Either way, we email you the Past Prospect Playbook.

How fast does it start?

We plan to launch within 30 days of kickoff, starting with your past prospects. The 90 days start at launch.

Do you promise new clients?

No. We commit to attended, qualified meetings. Closing them is yours.

Do you have RIA case studies?

Not yet. That is why the founding rate is below standard pricing, and why the commitment is written into your agreement.
